evidence.source: 王寧, “再說『白』字之本義,” 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心
evidence.text: The author reports that oracle-bone 白 was used for the color word 白, the title 伯, and a place name. He surveys proposals that the graph depicts cloth, a thumb, flame/light, a face or head, or a vessel, and rejects the thumb and head arguments as unproven. He then argues that 白 depicts an ancient cooking/measuring vessel 鬴/釜, with its middle stroke representing the joined lid and vessel; this is the author's own hypothesis, not an established consensus. He cautions that archaeological identification of an uninscribed vessel cannot establish what it was called in Shang times.
evidence.title: 王寧：再說“白”字之本義

evidence.source: 王寧, “再說『白』字之本義,” 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心
evidence.text: The article says oracle-bone examples use 白 for “white,” 伯, and a place name. Its author treats the white-color and lord/elder uses as phonetic loans, but the article also presents rival accounts of the graph's original referent. No dated individual inscription or securely reconstructed pronunciation of a depicted vessel is established on this page; the proposal therefore does not independently establish that vessel's name or sound.
evidence.title: 王寧：再說“白”字之本義

evidence.text: The entry presents oracle-bone, Western Zhou bronze, Warring States, seal, clerical and regular-script forms. It interprets the oracle-bone shape as a thumb with a fingerprint and says bronze and Warring States forms continue it; it describes the small-seal upper short stroke as arising from brush movement and the clerical/regular forms as increasingly obscuring the proposed original shape. This thumb reading is one account among disputed proposals, not independently verified here.
evidence.title: 白字形演变字源_汉字「白」

evidence.text: The page labels the charted forms Shang, Western Zhou, Shuowen/small seal, and Ming; it reports Mandarin bái (also bó) and gives competing comparative etymologies: STEDT's Proto-Sino-Tibetan *bawk analysis and Schuessler's alternative *bar with a -k extension, citing a medial-r mismatch in reconciling the former with Middle Chinese. These are word-etymology proposals, not accounts of graphic components. No sound component is proposed for 白 itself.

evidence.text: The entry indexes Shuowen Jiezi (Great Xu and Duan editions), Guangyun, and other historical dictionary witnesses for 白. Some listed witnesses are image links; this page's extracted text supplies their bibliographic labels but not their underlying definitions or readings.

gaps: No accessible source in this research established a consensus account of the original depicted object; thumb, cloth, light/flame, head/face, vessel, and other proposals remain disputed. The cited Fudan article advances the vessel hypothesis but explicitly notes the naming problem for archaeological objects.

The supplied Shuowen text gives Xu Shen's Han-era analysis (“from 入 joined with 二; 二 is the yin number”) and color definition, but this research did not inspect a primary Shuowen page or verify it against excavated early forms; treat it as a historical explanation, not confirmation of graphic origin.

The Fudan article reports oracle-bone uses for white, 伯, and a place name, but this research did not retrieve individually dated inscription contexts or establish when each semantic use began. Exact earliest attestation dates for the color sense, 伯/elder/title, and place-name use remain unresolved.

百 appears in the supplied dossier as an ancient use, but external pages inspected here did not establish its earliest attestation or a secure semantic link to 白. No chronology should be inferred from the order of glosses.
The source packet's candle/sun-rays explanation and its acorn hypothesis were not independently corroborated by the inspected primary or scholarly pages. They remain unsupported here.

Modern readings in the dossier were not independently checked across reference works. Wiktionary's opened page confirms Mandarin bái and also lists bó; historical phonological reconstructions in the dossier belong to different systems and cannot by themselves establish a depicted object's name.
The CUHK database result appeared in search results to describe a thumb and loan to the color word, but its page timed out when opened, so that claim is not counted as inspected evidence.
